threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line'—everyone here knows it's the one with the best street food nearby.
Last night, saw a guy serenading the bus with a ukulele. Got off at Stockwell, still strumming as he walked away, pure Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a couple casually fixing their bike in front of a café while a street artist painted a mural on the wall, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can order a beer at a kiosk in Friedrichshain at 8 AM, and no one bats an eye. It's a morning ritual for some locals.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their willingness to sprint for the 14 bus instead of waiting. It’s a trademark of survival here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 doing yoga during rush hour. Only in San Francisco would a bumpy bus ride turn into a Zen moment. Totally unfazed.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every café has Wi-Fi. In Gràcia, a lot of locals prefer to connect over coffee, not the internet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the T-10 tickets at the machines, while locals swipe their smartphones without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can find a parking spot on Lower Clapton Road after 6 PM without circling for ages. Welcome to reality!
Heard a group of lads on the 35 last night arguing about which chicken shop is the best in Brixton. Hilarious how passionate they got about it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The morning smell of fresh bagels from the corner shop mixed with the sound of a street performer playing on a broken guitar—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip coffee while dodging a spontaneous art installation made from old subway signs. It's part of the charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to carry a light jacket year-round—those fogs roll in unexpectedly, but tourists think it's always sunny. Classic S.F.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy using a broom as a makeshift microphone on the 49. He was belting out 'Don't Stop Believin''—Muni gold. The whole bus was singing along.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar in Gràcia serves tapas, but many still stick to vermut and olives. It's a whole vibe, not just food.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look confused by the menu at the local tapas bar, especially when they ask for ketchup with their patatas bravas.
